examples.content: Explain how QuickSort works with a simple example.

{"explanation":"Think of QuickSort like organizing a messy bookshelf. Pick one book as the 'pivot', put all shorter books to the left, taller to the right — then repeat on each side. With a good pivot, this divides work in half each time, giving us O(n log n) average performance.","mood":"explaining","code":{"language":"python","snippet":"def quick_sort(arr):
    if len(arr) <= 1:
        return arr
    pivot = arr[len(arr) // 2]  # middle element as pivot
    left = [x for x in arr if x < pivot]
    middle = [x for x in arr if x == pivot]
    right = [x for x in arr if x > pivot]
    return quick_sort(left) + middle + quick_sort(right)"},"visualSequence":{"type":"sorting","title":"QuickSort: Partition Around Pivot","steps":[{"step":1,"action":"highlight","description":"Select middle element as pivot","elements":[3]},{"step":2,"action":"compare","description":"Compare each element against pivot","elements":[0,3]},{"step":3,"action":"swap","description":"Move smaller elements left of pivot","elements":[1,5]},{"step":4,"action":"highlight","description":"Pivot is in its sorted position","elements":[3]},{"step":5,"action":"compare","description":"Recursively sort left and right sub-arrays","elements":[0,1]}]},"suggestedFollowUps":["What happens to QuickSort performance when the array is already sorted?","How does choosing a random pivot help avoid worst-case O(n²)?"]}

How does insertion work in an AVL Tree?

{"explanation":"An AVL tree is a self-balancing BST — after every insert, it checks if any node's left and right subtrees differ in height by more than 1. If unbalanced, it performs rotations to fix it. Think of it as a see-saw that auto-levels itself so searches stay O(log n) always.","mood":"explaining","code":{"language":"python","snippet":"class AVLNode:
    def __init__(self, key):
        self.key = key
        self.left = self.right = None
        self.height = 1

def get_height(node):
    return node.height if node else 0

def get_balance(node):
    return get_height(node.left) - get_height(node.right) if node else 0

def rotate_right(z):
    y = z.left
    T3 = y.right
    y.right = z
    z.left = T3
    z.height = 1 + max(get_height(z.left), get_height(z.right))
    y.height = 1 + max(get_height(y.left), get_height(y.right))
    return y"},"visualSequence":{"type":"tree","title":"AVL Tree Insertion & Rotation","steps":[{"step":1,"action":"insert","description":"Insert new node like a standard BST","elements":[5]},{"step":2,"action":"traverse","description":"Walk back up to root checking balance factors","elements":[4,3,2]},{"step":3,"action":"highlight","description":"Node at index 2 is unbalanced (balance > 1)","elements":[2]},{"step":4,"action":"swap","description":"Perform right rotation to restore balance","elements":[1,2]},{"step":5,"action":"highlight","description":"Tree is balanced — all heights updated","elements":[0,1,2,3,4,5]}]},"suggestedFollowUps":["What are the four rotation cases in AVL Trees?","How does a Red-Black Tree differ from an AVL Tree in rebalancing?"]}
